newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Less liquid Russian stocks sought in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Less liquid Russian stocks sought in quiet trade.

text.p: Leading Russian shares were little changed little on Tuesday, and traders said investors were shifting funds into less liquid stocks.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 356.44, barely changed from Monday's closing 356.52.
Traders gave mixed opions as to where the market would move during the day, but said prices would change little.
"In the morning everyone put out bids, but withdrew them quickly for lack of support," said IFCI-Moscow Partners corporate securities head Dmitry Voronkov.

"Now everything is very quiet. Maybe something will change when London and New York open. I think most likely there will be some selling. I cannot see any new money and investors prefer to transfer old money into less liquid paper."
Creditanstalt-Grant chief trader Andrei Galperin forecast a slight rise after Monday's U.S. and UK market holidays.
"Maybe the market will edge up a bit. Money is coming in again," he said. "I am not saying there will be a rise, as almost 90 percent of funds are now in second and third-tier shares."
National power utility UES fell to $0.3165 at 1000 GMT from $0.3198, Rostelekom slipped to $3.85 from $3.86, Surgutneftegaz fell to $0.84 from $0.86.
Traders said news the government planned to sell shares in telecoms holding AO Svyazinvest, and Surgutneftegaz's plans to issue new shares failed to have an impact on the market.

"As for Svyazinvest... the most important thing now is how the authorised capital will be formed. But I think that many people now think they should sell Rostelekom and buy Svyazinvest," Galperin said.
